title: A clipped multi-line string in a list that replaces a literal block stays a literal block
notes: The value of `a` is a literal block scalar followed by an empty line and the next entry. It is replaced by a list with one string, `make` and one final line break. Reading the result back must give that list. The specification allows a double-quoted item (`- "make\n"`) as well as a literal one, so the exact bytes rest on the kit convention listed in docs/edit-semantics.md: a string whose only line break is its last, set where a literal block scalar was, is written as a literal block with clip chomping, not quoted. The empty line before `b` is not content of the string (YAML 1.2.2 section 8.1.3: with clip chomping the final line break is kept and trailing empty lines are not content) and stays where it was, byte for byte.

provenance.reference: A patch engine that quoted every item of a list built to replace a literal block scalar when an empty line followed the scalar.
